findings.condition: A future production deployment sets a secret-like value on a NEXT_PUBLIC_* environment variable whose name does not contain the literal substrings SECRET|TOKEN|PASSWORD|RECOVERY|DATABASE (e.g. NEXT_PUBLIC_SQUARE_APIKEY, NEXT_PUBLIC_STORAGE_CREDENTIAL, NEXT_PUBLIC_SIGNING_CERT).
findings.impact: The defense-in-depth guard in secretMetadataFromEnvironment does not fire for these names, giving false assurance that 'public secret variables' are rejected. It does not itself leak anything (the function only validates ZAO_PRODUCTION_SECRET_METADATA), but an operator relying on this check as a safety net for accidental NEXT_PUBLIC_ secret exposure would not be warned for a plausible class of variable names.
findings.fix: Broaden the heuristic (add API[_-]?KEY, CREDENTIAL, CERT, PRIVATE, ACCESS to the alternation) or, better, replace the denylist with an explicit allowlist of permitted NEXT_PUBLIC_* names and document this check as heuristic defense-in-depth rather than the primary control.
findings.test: Add a case to tests/unit/production-integration.test.ts asserting secretMetadataFromEnvironment throws when e.g. NEXT_PUBLIC_SQUARE_APIKEY is set alongside a valid ZAO_PRODUCTION_SECRET_METADATA payload.

findings.condition: restoreOwnedCluster starts EmbeddedPostgres against a data directory that was byte-for-byte copied from the original stopped cluster (which already contains its own role/password material), while passing a freshly generated random `password` to the constructor; the pool actually authenticates afterward using `backup.auth.password` (the original captured credential) at line 33.
findings.impact: No functional or security defect is demonstrated here (evidence shows the restore tests pass), but the code misleadingly implies the restore path rotates/sets a new database password, which could mislead a future maintainer into believing credential rotation occurs during restore, or mask a real regression if a future embedded-postgres upgrade begins honoring this field on non-initialising starts.
findings.evidence: line 32: `password:randomBytes(24).toString('hex')` inside the EmbeddedPostgres constructor for a `persistent:true`, already-initialized copied directory, versus line 33 `new Pool({host:'127.0.0.1',port:identity.dbPort,...backup.auth})` which uses the original pre-stop credential.
findings.fix: Either drop the misleading `password` field (or pass `backup.auth.password` explicitly for consistency) and add a one-line comment that this field is inert for a start against pre-initialized data, to prevent confusion about whether restore performs credential rotation.
findings.test: No new test strictly required; optionally add an assertion that connecting to the restored cluster with a deliberately wrong password fails, pinning that the copied original credential (not the constructor's password field) is authoritative.

insufficient_evidence: Whether .local/backup-drill/ and other .local/* paths used by scripts/isolated-backup.ts are excluded via .gitignore from Git/CI artifacts, as asserted in docs/adr/0029 and PRODUCTION_P2_RUNBOOK.md — no .gitignore content or diff was included in the reviewed snapshot.

Internal behavior of the third-party `embedded-postgres` package regarding the `password` constructor option when starting (not initializing) an already-provisioned data directory — inferred correct/inert only from passing test evidence, not from library source, which was not supplied.
